findings.claim: Analysts see multi-year deficits in U.S. transformer supply persisting even as manufacturers invest billions in new capacity; 2026 market demand is projected to beat 2024 levels by 21% for power transformers and 16% for GSUs (generator step-up transformers), and lead times for high-capacity transformers now reach three to four years versus roughly one year in 2020-2021, with high-voltage circuit breakers reaching ~125 weeks.
findings.source: POWER Magazine, "Transformers in 2026: Shortage, Scramble, or Self-Inflicted Crisis?"

findings.claim: The grid-equipment constraint is characterized as structural rather than purely cyclical: data center load growth, grid upgrades, renewable interconnection, industrial electrification, and utility replacement cycles are all competing for the same transformer, switchgear, and breaker manufacturing capacity, with deficits expected to persist through at least 2030.
findings.source: eepower.com / Environment+Energy Leader coverage on grid equipment bottleneck (aggregated from Wood Mackenzie and RMI supply-chain analysis)

findings.claim: Major manufacturers including Hitachi Energy (>$1B including a $457M Virginia plant targeting largest-in-nation capacity by 2028), Siemens Energy ($150M Charlotte NC plant, production start early 2027), and Eaton itself ($340M three-phase transformer facility in South Carolina, targeting a 2027 start) are all adding new large-power-transformer capacity, meaning meaningful new supply begins arriving 2027-2028.
findings.source: POWER Magazine, "Transformers in 2026: Shortage, Scramble, or Self-Inflicted Crisis?"

findings.claim: Global power transformer market is estimated at $28.2B in 2026, forecast to reach $46.4B by 2033 (7.4% CAGR); data center electricity consumption (about 4.4% of U.S. electricity in 2023) is projected to double or triple by 2028, and in April 2026 the U.S. invoked the Defense Production Act to boost domestic transformer/substation/high-voltage component manufacturing, with DOE allocating $375M in January 2026 to strengthen the transformer supply chain.
findings.source: Future Market Insights transformer market report; IEA "Building the Future Transmission Grid" supply-chain report

findings.claim: The U.S. power/distribution transformer industry (which Eaton participates in) faces an unprecedented supply-demand imbalance; a key structural bottleneck is grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES) — there is only one domestic U.S. GOES manufacturer, domestic GOES supply can meet only about 20% of U.S. transformer demand, and over 90% of high-grade GOES production capacity is concentrated in China, Japan and South Korea (China alone holds over 56% of global GOES production capacity).
findings.source: PowerMag 'Transformers in 2026: Shortage, Scramble, or Self-Inflicted Crisis?'; ChinaTalk 'Gridlocked: Transformer Shortage Choking U.S. Supply Chains'

findings.claim: China's exports of high-power transformers surged 61% year-on-year in January-February 2026 (exports to the U.S. up 182%), and Goldman Sachs raised its forecast for U.S. transformer import dependency to 60%, with transformer lead times extended from roughly 12 months historically to 48-60 months and manufacturer capacity effectively sold out through the end of the decade — indicating the U.S. transformer supply chain (Eaton's core Electrical segment input/output category) remains structurally dependent on a geographically concentrated (China-heavy) upstream steel and finished-transformer supply base.
findings.source: Futu News 'Global Transformer Shortage! China's exports surge 61%...'; ChinaTalk 'Gridlocked: Transformer Shortage Choking U.S. Supply Chains'

findings.claim: In response to the transformer/switchgear supply crunch, Eaton has invested more than $1.5 billion in global manufacturing capacity since 2023, including a specific $340 million investment to increase U.S. production of three-phase transformers, plus a new transformer manufacturing site in South Carolina and increased U.S.-made medium-voltage switchgear production, aimed at meeting data-center-driven demand and reducing reliance on constrained external transformer supply.
findings.source: RenewableEnergyWorld 'Eaton increases US-made medium-voltage switchgear production to help meet data center demand'; Eaton press release 'Eaton invests in new South Carolina transformer manufacturing site' (eaton.com)

findings.claim: Solid-state transformers (SST) are emerging as a substitute technology for traditional oil-filled/magnetic transformers, offering bidirectional power flow, real-time voltage regulation and compact footprint that conventional units cannot match; utilities, data center owners, rail operators and EV charging providers are driving adoption. The global SST market is projected to grow from roughly $170-205M in 2026 toward $360-380M by 2031-2033 (CAGR ~13%).
findings.source: Mordor Intelligence / MarketsandMarkets / Coherent Market Insights solid-state transformer market reports

findings.claim: Delta Electronics deployed its solid-state transformer system (using SiC high-frequency power conversion) at a hyperscale data center campus in North China in February 2026, in partnership with Chindata Group and Meituan, targeting the same AI-data-center power delivery use case Eaton competes for.
findings.source: Solid-State Transformer Market industry report coverage (researchdive/Cervicorn Insights aggregation)

findings.claim: Eaton completed the acquisition of Resilient Power Systems Inc. on 2025-08-06 (announced July 2025, ~$86M: $55M cash + $31M estimated contingent consideration) to bring medium-voltage solid-state transformer technology in-house, directly addressing the SST substitution threat rather than being displaced by it.
findings.source: Eaton press release "Eaton completes acquisition of Resilient Power Systems Inc., strengthening power distribution offerings"

findings.claim: Eaton guided to first orders for its own solid-state transformer systems in H2 2026, with shipments starting late 2027; analysis frames Eaton's strategy as trying to become a "grid-to-chip" integration platform for AI infrastructure (via Boyd Thermal, an 800V DC pilot programme, an NVIDIA Vera Rubin/Beam partnership, and a Siemens Energy tie-up) rather than remaining a component-only electrical equipment incumbent, in response to Schneider Electric's downstream integration advantage.
findings.source: electroneconomics.substack.com, "Eaton is trying to become Schneider before the AI factory standardises" (citing Eaton 8-K exhibits)

sections.supply:
PART III · SUPPLY SIDE
 供給側：電力鎖死供給，利潤遷往互連
 反直覺但可操作：電力瓶頸是這輪資本週期的朋友——它把過剩風險從 2026 推到 2028+；同時利潤正從「蓋大箱子」遷往「互連 + 已能源化 colo」兩端。

 供給分三層房東：公開雙寡占 DLR + EQIX（合計公開市值 ~$175-180B）、私募大型化（Blackstone QTS 自 2021 租出 MW 擴約 14 倍、Vantage/Aligned/CyrusOne/Compass）、與超大廠自建（Stargate ~7 GW、Meta Hyperion 5 GW、Prometheus 1 GW）。瓶頸不在水泥鋼筋、在電力與資金成本：北維吉尼亞併網最多 7 年、德州 CenterPoint 大型負載申請一年內 1→8 GW（+700%）、ISO 承認排隊發電僅約 2 成真的在蓋。成本曲線以「電力可得性 / 資金成本曲線」取代物理成本曲線（DC REIT 是租賃地產、無實體產能邊際成本）：已能源化的 incumbent 在曲線最左（最快變現），純排隊新進者在最右（5-7 年才交付）；價格戰終局不由邊際成本決定、由「誰有電可賣」決定。

 
 Inference · 供給
 已能源化土地的稀缺，新進者 2028 前 physically 補不上
 前提：併網 5-7 年 + 變壓器交期數年 + 排隊發電僅 ~2 成在蓋 + 約 6 成次年容量準時交付
 即使資金狂湧（超大廠 2026 total capex ~$600B+），產能上線仍有結構性時滯——這把過剩風險從 2026 推到 2028+。掌握「已通電土地」的 incumbent（DLR 5 GW runway、EQIX 核心都會）享最持久的稀缺租金；但同一枷鎖也封住自己的增量。
 可證偽條件：若聯邦/州電力法案 + BTM SMR 2027-28 商用 + 電網投資加速，使 grid lead time 縮至 < 2 年，則「電力 moat」失效、過剩風險前移。
 

 
 利潤池遷移 · 毛利率為各家最新季 T1 / 定性
 
環節 | 毛利 / 利潤池 | 遷移 | 搶 / 被搶
上游：電力 / 設備 | VRT/GEV ~25-35% | ↑ | 交期數年→寡占
中游：DC REIT 批發 colo | ~50-55% gross | → | 利差最薄、被超大廠議價
中游：DC REIT 零售 + 互連 | ~70-75% gross | ↑↑ | 利潤池最肥、最持久
下游：hyperscaler tenant | ~20-35%（雲端） | ↓ / 剛 | 對批發升、對互連弱
邊緣：私募 / neocloud | CRWV 槓桿高 | → | 以債換 backlog、信用前置

 
 怎麼讀：利潤往「零售 + 互連」集中（~70-75% gross 且 ↑↑），因 cross-connect 移轉成本極高、推論越分散越依賴 fabric。批發 colo 雖是多頭故事主角，但毛利與 cap rate 都被超大廠議價力壓、利差最薄——這正是 KEY CALL「選錯了段」。信用鏈順序：AI 循環若斷一環，neocloud → 私募 → 最後才到公開 REIT，給雙寡占時間緩衝。
sections.demand:
PART IV · DEMAND SIDE
 需求側：超大廠 capex 與 MW 吸納的對帳
 最剛性的是 AI 推論（要低 latency、分散部署，2026 已從 pilot 轉 production）；最脆弱的是「超大廠把推論也收回自建」的長尾風險。本節用超大廠 capex 對帳實體 MW 吸納，判斷需求是否撐得起估值。

 2026 四大（AMZN/GOOGL/META/MSFT）total capex 估計 ~$520-560B、含 ORCL 等五大則達 ~$600-630B（口徑不一、YoY 約 +40-62%；來源 IEEE ComSoc / CreditSights，非四大窄義 PP&E），約 75% 投向 AI 基建；對應端是北美 2025 全年淨吸納創紀錄 2,497.6 MW。需求 mix 三層：超大廠 anchor（簽 100 MW+ 長約、批發 colo 命脈）＞ AI-native（OpenAI 走 Stargate 自建為主、Anthropic/xAI 走 colo + cloud）＞ 企業（出現 100 MW 級 AI deals）。DLR 2026-Q1 的 0-1MW + 互連 bookings 創 $98M 紀錄（+40% YoY、21% AI），證明分散式推論需求正實體落地。

 
 需求三角驗證 · top-down vs bottom-up（口徑不同，量級判斷）
 
層 | 數值 | 口徑
下游 capex（bottom-up） | 四大 ~$520-560B；含 ORCL 等五大 ~$600-630B | 曆年 total capex guidance（口徑不一、T1 法說）
實體 MW 吸納 | 2025 淨吸納 2,497.6 MW 創高 | CBRE 即時市場數據（T2）
colo TAM（top-down） | 2030 ~$165-205B | 研究機構口徑（CAGR 11-16%）

 
 怎麼讀：上游 capex（~$600B、需求存在的鐵證、非直接 colo 營收）vs「2,500 MW × ~$9-12M/MW ≈ $25-30B colo 增量」差約一個數量級，但合理——capex 絕大多是 GPU/伺服器/網路與超大廠自建（不進 colo TAM），真正流進房東的只是「租賃」那一小片。推導：colo base ~$200B（2025 $104B ×（1+14%）^5）；bull ~$230B（CAGR→16%）、bear ~$165B（CAGR→11%）。採信哪邊？短期採信 bottom-up 的實體 MW 吸納 + 預租率（最硬最即時），TAM 數字當區間參考。

 
 Inference · 需求
 需求剛、但要選對段——互連 > 已能源化批發
 前提：推論需低 latency + 分散 + 多雲互連 + token 量爆炸（瓦特剛性）
 推論需求的微觀引擎是 token 經濟學——量爆炸但單價崩，AI 營收靠能力階梯 + agentic 乘數硬撐；但跑 token 要的是「瓦特」不是「美元」，故實體算力載體需求剛性。二階效應：每 1 GW DC 需 ~1 GW 發電+變電+輸電，把需求灌進公用事業/變壓器/電力電子/鈾——需求與護城河同源。
 可證偽條件：若 MSFT/AMZN/GOOG/META 任一在 2026 Q3-Q4 宣告推論自建 > 50% 容量，「推論進 colo」thesis 立即降信心。
 

 
 多空為何都對
 多頭測的是供給緊俏（空置率、租金、吸納），空頭測的是需求變現（token 單價、企業 ROI、自建蔓延）——兩者測的不是同一件事，可同時為真：算力載體確實被吃滿（多頭對），但終端變現能否長期跟上、超大廠會不會把推論也收回自建仍待驗（空頭對）。本報告因此把重心放在「電力鎖死能撐多久 + 哪一段是真 alpha」。
